name: Medellín
tagline: The City of Eternal Spring Where Your Dollar Blooms
description: Medellín delivers arguably the best value proposition in Latin America for FIRE retirees — perfect year-round weather, dramatically low costs, excellent private healthcare, and a booming innovation scene. Once infamous, the city has transformed into a global hotspot for digital nomads and early retirees seeking first-world amenities at developing-world prices.

quickFacts.visa: Colombia Retirement Visa (Visa M - Jubilado; requires pension or income ~$750/mo, renewable annually)
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate — very safe in El Poblado, Laureles, Envigado; standard urban caution elsewhere
quickFacts.climate: Tropical highland — eternal spring, 70-82°F year-round with two rainy seasons

housing.description: Modest furnished studio / small 1BR in a safe non-prime area (Belén, Envigado/Sabaneta edge, or Laureles periphery); respects the expat-safe floor

dining.description: Menú del día lunches a few times a week plus casual eats; mostly home cooking

healthcare.description: Mandatory EPS contribution plus an optional entry local plan; 45–55 basis

transportation.description: Metro plus integrated bus, occasional Uber; no car

entertainment.description: Parks, Pueblito Paisa, free cultural events, occasional cinema

1M.lifestyle: A modest furnished studio or compact one-bedroom in a safe, well-connected barrio — Laureles' quieter edges, Belén, or up toward Envigado — anchors a frugal but genuinely pleasant routine. Most meals come from neighborhood markets and home cooking, with the inexpensive menú del día handling lunches out. Getting around is the clean, cheap Metro and its cable-car and bus network, with an occasional Uber and no car needed. The spring-like climate erases heating and cooling bills entirely, and the city's parks and free cultural programming do the entertaining. Careful and lean, but comfortable, with basic public-plus-entry-private cover for routine care.

housing.description: Furnished 1BR in a desirable, walkable area (solid Laureles, El Poblado-adjacent, or good Envigado), amenity building

dining.description: Out 3–4x/week mixing local comida with mid-range Laureles/Poblado tables

healthcare.description: EPS plus a private prepagada plan (Colsanitas or Sura) for fast specialist access

transportation.description: Metro plus regular Uber; still no car

entertainment.description: A fuller cultural/social calendar plus a gym

2M.lifestyle: A comfortable furnished apartment in Laureles or an El Poblado-adjacent block puts cafés, the Estadio nightlife, and leafy streets on the doorstep. Eating out three or four nights a week across the city's easy casual-to-mid scene becomes routine, and a private prepagada plan layered over EPS opens quick access to Medellín's strong private hospitals. The Metro plus habitual rideshare covers the valley end to end. A gym membership and a steady calendar of concerts, markets, and day trips round out an unpretentious, easy life with money to spare.

housing.description: Quality furnished 1BR in prime El Poblado (near the Golden Mile) or the best of Laureles; modern amenity building

dining.description: Dining out most days across the Poblado/Laureles scene

healthcare.description: Top prepagada (Colsanitas/Sura) with full access to leading private hospitals; approaching an entry international plan

transportation.description: Uber-heavy daily use plus occasional car rental; car ownership optional

entertainment.description: Rich cultural, dining, and regional-travel calendar

3M.lifestyle: A quality furnished apartment in prime El Poblado near the Golden Mile — or the best of Laureles — anchors a confident, unhurried FIRE routine in an amenity building with pool and gym. Dining out is near-daily across an acclaimed and still-affordable restaurant scene, groceries lean on premium supermarkets and imported specialties, and a top prepagada plan keeps out-of-pocket exposure low with full access to Medellín's best private hospitals. Rideshare-first mobility handles the city, with weekend escapes to Guatapé, the coffee region, or the Caribbean coast easily in budget. A full calendar of theatre, fine dining, and cultural memberships comes with real margin left over.

housing.description: Luxury amenity apartment in prime El Poblado (Golden Mile / El Tesoro) or top Laureles — doorman, pool, gym, concierge

dining.description: Near-daily dining including the city's top tables, with occasional destination fine dining

healthcare.description: Top-tier prepagada plus an entry international plan (Cigna Global / Allianz) with regional coverage

entertainment.description: Premium leisure, wellness, and travel routine

5M.lifestyle: A luxury amenity apartment on El Poblado's Golden Mile or up in El Tesoro — doorman, rooftop pool, mountain views — sets the tone, with a housekeeper coming two or three days a week. Dining spans casual to Medellín's celebrated destination tables without a second thought, an entry-level international plan adds cross-border coverage on top of premium local care, and an owned car plus premium rideshare cover the valley. Discretionary spend flows into wellness, cultural memberships, and frequent getaways. Comfortably clear of what daily life requires, with the surplus going to travel and savings.

housing.description: Prime furnished penthouse on the El Poblado Golden Mile / El Tesoro, or an estate in the Las Palmas / El Retiro hills — top of the long-term luxury stock

dining.description: Near-daily fine dining across the city's best plus entertaining

healthcare.description: International concierge plan with medical evacuation to Miami/Houston; 45–55 basis

transportation.description: Owned luxury car plus frequent private driver

entertainment.description: Lavish entertaining, private events, premium memberships, frequent travel, wellness

domesticHelp.description: Full-time live-out staff (housekeeper-cook plus part-time driver-caretaker)

luxuryExtras.description: Frequent international travel, art/wine, exclusive club memberships, luxury shopping

10M.lifestyle: A trophy penthouse on the Golden Mile or a gated estate in the cool Las Palmas–El Retiro hills — private terrace, valley views, kept by full-time staff including a housekeeper-cook and an on-call driver. Fine dining is near-daily at the destination tables that have put this city on the culinary map, and an international concierge plan with cross-border medical evacuation removes the last friction. A luxury vehicle with private driving, gourmet and imported provisioning, and a discretionary budget for constant travel, art, and elite club memberships mean nothing is out of reach. This is Medellín at its most opulent — an exclusive address, resident staff, and a world-class private-medicine city at the door.
